inference.made_by: backup/how-big-is-one-step-of-a-gain.py, backup/read-the-cut-side-again.py, backup/does-the-dent-move-with-the-width.py, backup/the-tone-control-nobody-prints.py, backup/build-gain-models.py, backup/run-gain-reproduce.py, backup/where-the-dent-lives.py, backup/write-gain-inference.py

claim: A gain byte printed -12 - +12 is decibels, one per step, offset by sixty-four. It answers over a window of twenty-five values from 52 to 76 and returns the nearest end for everything outside. And the two of them that forty-three types carry with no frequency printed beside either are this unit's equaliser's own shelf pair with the frequency byte taken away and pinned to its first printed entry.
why_not_named: There is nothing to name. The claim is a mapping from a byte to a number and a statement that two addresses on forty-three types are one filter measured elsewhere; neither is a structure with a name.

measurements.why: All twenty-five live settings of one gain byte and two past each end, read on a peaking section at its widest width and centred where the band set is densest, so what the profile is largest by is the gain and not a flank of it. This is the only record in the archive that asks the byte at every setting it answers at.

The cut half read a second time into the same take store, against the same reference. Whether a departure from the step law is the machine's or the evening's is not a thing a single pass can say, and the run that found the departure did not ask.

Four mirrored pairs at the width one entry along from the one the departure was found at. A stored decibel does not know what width the section is at, so a departure that moves when the width does is not in the table.

The low gain of a type whose page prints no frequency against it, with the type's modulator parked and its pre-filter off so the chain is the tone control and a delay line. Forty-three types carry this address.
The other half of the same tone control, on the same takes.
The equaliser's low shelf at full boost, at each of the two corners its page prints. Held against the tone control's profile band for band, with no model between them.
The same for the high shelf.

documents.why: A hundred and eighteen parameters are printed -12 - +12 and eighty-six of them are a Low Gain and a Hi Gain at the same two offsets of forty-three types, with no frequency, width or order printed against either. That is what makes this a class rather than two addresses, and it is evidence about a page and not about a unit.

era_priors.claim: A filter gain is not one number the way an output level is, so a table of gains is a table of coefficient sets and costs what it costs multiplied by every frequency and every width the same section offers.
era_priors.why: Twenty-five gains against sixteen centres and five widths is two thousand entries, and nothing of the period spends that on a tone control. But the coefficients are recomputed when a parameter changes and not per sample, so the control processor can afford here the arithmetic the audio path could not -- which is the opposite of what the same period implies about an output level, where the table is a hundred and twenty-eight bytes and a formula buys nothing.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The measured decibels landed on a grid coarse enough to be a stored table rather than on the integers. They land on the integers on the boost half to a tenth of a decibel, and the one setting that does not lands back on them at another width.

era_priors.claim: A control marked in decibels steps in decibels, and twenty-five settings out of a hundred and twenty-eight means something maps a printed range onto a stretch of the byte and refuses the rest.
era_priors.why: Where that stretch sits is measurable rather than arguable, and this unit's other classes have already turned out to work that way: a width byte with five entries that returns the first for anything past them, a rate byte whose last two settings have no entry of their own.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The byte went on answering outside 52 to 76. Three settings past each end return the same figure as the end itself.

adds: The records say what each setting of a gain byte did to the level of each band. Nothing in them says the byte is decibels, that it is one per step, where the window is, that a departure at one setting belongs to the section rather than to the table, or that two addresses on forty-three types are a filter this archive has already measured somewhere else. Each of those is a comparison across records and the comparisons are made here: a boost half against the integers, a cut half against itself at two widths, and a tone control against an equaliser's shelves band for band.

the_window.what: The byte answers from 52 to 76 and sticks at both ends, measured on a third address and now on a section whose whole gain is inside the band set.
the_window.read_as: Three settings at each end within a twentieth of a decibel of each other. The printed range is the byte's range and not a recommendation.

the_step.what: One decibel per step, read as the height of the feature at a twelfth of an octave, where the rendered chain and the unit go through the same band set and whatever it takes off the top of a broad peak it takes off both.
the_step.read_as: The boost half is the law. The cut half is not, and the whole of the difference between the two halves is where this class stops.

the_second_pass.what: The cut half read again, setting by setting, against the same reference.

and_one_that_did_not.why: One take of setting 62 came back with every band of its profile about a decibel down, from a hundred hertz to twelve and a half kilohertz. A byte that moves one peaking section cannot do that, so what moved was the take. It is named rather than dropped: a departure that is a broadband shift and one that is localised to the feature are different things, and only the second is a reading of this byte.

the_second_pass.read_as: The departures repeat. Setting 55 comes back within a fiftieth of a decibel of where it was, which is what makes it a measurement and not an evening.

where_the_departure_lives.what: The dented setting and its mirror, and three clean pairs beside them, read again at another width. One scale per width is fitted across all eight settings first, because how much of the peak a band catches changes when the width does and that is not the section's gain.
where_the_departure_lives.read_as: Setting 55 sits 0.40 dB off the law at the width it was found at and 0.06 one along -- it lands back on the law. Nothing else moves by more than 0.18. A stored decibel does not know the width, so what is dented is how the section realises a cut and not what the byte stands for. The margin over the loudest of the seven controls is 1.88, which is under two and is why this is written as where the departure is not rather than as what it is.

the_tone_control_no_page_describes.what: The two gains that forty-three types carry, at full boost, held band for band against this unit's equaliser's own shelves at full boost, at each of the two corners the equaliser's page prints. Two measurements against each other with no model between them.
the_tone_control_no_page_describes.read_as: The low gain matches the first printed corner to a median 0.03 dB and a worst 0.06 over twenty-two bands, and the other corner by 0.4 and 3.26. The high gain: 0.02 and 0.05 against the first, 0.215 and 4.37 against the other. Two different effect types, two different chains, one profile. The generic tone control is the equaliser's shelf pair with the frequency byte removed and held at its first entry, which gives forty-three types a filter out of records that already existed.

and_its_cut.why: The shelf's cut at the bottom of the byte against its boost at the top, negated. On this section the two are mirrors, which is what the peaking section at one of its widths is not.

alternatives.reading: The multiplier steps evenly across the byte and the decibels are whatever that lands on, which is what a section built as a scaled band-pass summed with the dry gives.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Read as the height of the feature it is out by a mean 0.046 of the span against 0.010 for the step law, and its worst record is 0.170 against 0.032. Read over the whole profile it comes first on the median and leans on 3 records where the step law leans on 0. Coming first while leaning is being beaten, and it is beaten under the reading the class's own quantity lives in.

alternatives.reading: The byte is decibels offset by sixty-four over all hundred and twenty-eight settings and the printed range is where the panel stops.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Three settings past each end of the window return the same figure as the end itself, to within a twentieth of a decibel, on a section that reads the gain rather than a flank of it. The byte does not reach sixty-four decibels of cut; it stops at twelve and stays there.

alternatives.reading: The twenty-five settings are a stored table of near-decibels rather than the integers, and the departures on the cut half are its entries.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The largest departure is at one setting and it is gone at another width, where the same setting lands on the law. An entry of a table cannot depend on the width byte. What is left after that is a boost half on the law to 0.15 dB and a cut half whose remaining departures are two tenths, which is what one of these readings resolves at the peak and is not a table.

separated_by.observable: Whether a departure repeats at the same byte across widths, centres and sections.
separated_by.what_the_run_returned: Four mirrored pairs at two widths. The one that departs at the first width lands on the law at the second and nothing else moves by half as much.
separated_by.why_not_separable: Only for the departures under two tenths of a decibel, which are the size of what this reading resolves at the peak band. Telling a table of near-decibels from the integers there needs a reading finer than a twelfth-octave band profile of a held note, and the archive has already measured that reading finer scatters rather than sharpens on this type.

alternatives.reading: A peaking section's cut is its boost inverted, so mirrored settings have the same height.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It holds on the shelves and not on the peaking sections. The tone control's cut is its boost negated to a median 0.02 dB over twenty-two bands. The peaking section's mirrored pair at nine decibels is 0.46 dB apart at one width and 0.14 at another, where its other three pairs are within a quarter of a decibel at both. One structure inverted cannot be apart at all, and cannot be apart by an amount that changes with the width.

refuted_by: A setting inside 52 to 76 whose gain is not the byte minus sixty-four decibels by more than a fifth of one, on a section that reads the gain rather than a flank, at more than one width. Or a type whose Low Gain profile at full boost is not the equaliser's low shelf at its first printed corner.

compared_against.generated_from: data/units/roland-sc8850-01/index.json, filtered to the efx-bands records of type 01 00 whose swept address is one of the four printed -12 - +12, at the finest resolution published for each

excluded.why: The second type. Its records are held against this one record to record with no model between them, which is stated under the_tone_control_no_page_describes; a comparison of two measurements is not a model's comparison set. The models here are chains of this type and cannot be rendered for another.

domain.outside: Every type but two, and on the second only the two ends of each gain. The eight bands of the graphic equaliser, which print the same range against something this claim says nothing about. Any pair of gains moved together: one byte at a time throughout.

residual.unit: share of the span the effect commands in that record
residual.why: Read as the height of the feature, off both sides of the same band set. The floor is the run's own spread at the bands the feature was largest in, which on the fullest record is a quarter of a decibel, and the model leans against it on five of the nine records.

also_read_as.unit: share of the span, over every band of the profile
also_read_as.why: The archive's default reading. It is mostly skirt on this class -- the quantity sits in two or three bands out of twenty-two -- and under it the step law leans on none of the nine records while the multiplier candidate ranks first and leans on three.

gross.why: The median residual over the span the effect commands, taken as the worst of the records scored. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

qualitative.why: Properties the unit's readings have that the model's readings must have too. No arithmetic over a residual rescues a model that cuts where the unit boosts.

power.why: The runner-up in the catalogue, scored on the same records, and whether it leans or contradicts a property where the winner does neither. The decoy is not chosen -- it is whichever candidate came second, so a strawman cannot be put up in its place. A class holding one candidate is a catalogue that is unfinished, which is a finding and not a pass.

records_the_run_did_not_reach.why: The profile had not levelled off where the band set ended, so the corner the model takes from this record is a lower bound. A residual leaning across the bands is that bound leaning. Answering it needs a stimulus that reaches further, not a different model.

reproduces.what_survived_twice: One candidate and no verdict. `decibels-are-the-byte-minus-sixty-four` is the ranking's winner read as a height and the only candidate that does not lean read as a profile; the multiplier candidate is beaten under the first and leans under the second. Neither reading returns `reproduces` for anything, so the class stands on the mapping and does not close on the model. What stops it is stated and is not the byte: the model renders a peaking cut as the exact mirror of its boost and this unit does not, which is a topology this class is not about and the equaliser class now carries as an open reading.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Whether the peaking sections' cut branch is the boost branch inverted. It is not, by up to half a decibel at one setting of one width, and what it is instead is not read here. That is the equaliser's topology and not this class's mapping, and it is why neither reading of this class returns `reproduces`.
what_this_does_not_close.bounded_by: Four mirrored pairs at two widths on one section. Three of the four are within a quarter of a decibel at both widths, so whatever the asymmetry is, it is not a constant and it is under the reading's own floor over most of the byte.

what_this_does_not_close.what: The eight bands of the graphic equaliser. Eight gains printed -12 - +12 with no frequency, width or count printed against any of them.
what_this_does_not_close.bounded_by: Nothing measured. The claim's addresses do not include them and the class does not reach them.

what_this_does_not_close.what: Whether the forty-one other types that carry the two gains carry the same shelves. Two are measured and they agree.
what_this_does_not_close.bounded_by: The two measured are as unlike each other as this address gets -- four filter sections and a delay line with a modulator -- and their profiles agree to within what the run resolves. A third would cost four minutes and the queue says so.

what_it_would_change: A hundred and eighteen parameters across sixty-five types stop being unknown. Eighty-six of them are two shelves whose corners no page prints and which now have a measured profile at both of their gains' ends, taken from a type that does print its corners. A renderer that has the equaliser has the tone control.
